in_arabic.name: عبيد
in_arabic.long_meaning: عبيد هو اسم عربي معناه الخادم الحبيب والمسلم اللطيف، ويستخدم في الإسلام لوصف شخص من العبيد الذين استقروا على الإسلام ويقدرون على أداء الواجبات، ويُعتبر عبيد من أسماء الإلهية في الإسلام، ويُستخدم أيضا لوصف العبد الحبيب الذي يعمل على طاعة الله، وتأتي جذور هذا الاسم من الحرفين عب ويد، والذي يعني الخدمة والتعاون، ويتضمن عبيد معنى الخدمة والعمل الجاد في الطاعة، وتظهر جذور هذا الاسم في القرآن الكريم في سورة التوبة الآية 25، ويتضمن عبيد أيضا معنى الحب والانتماء، حيث يُعتبر العبد الحبيب الذي يعمل على طاعة الله، ويتضمن عبيد أيضا معنى الجود والكرم، حيث يُعتبر الخادم الحبيب الذي يعمل على طاعة الله، ويتضمن عبيد أيضا معنى الإخلاص والانتماء، حيث يُعتبر العبد الحبيب الذي يعمل على طاعة الله، وفي التقاليد الإسلامية يُعتبر عبيد اسمًا مقدسًا ويُستخدم في تسمية الأطفال، ويُعتبر عبيد من أسماء الإلهية في الإسلام، ويُستخدم أيضا لوصف العبد الحبيب الذي يعمل على طاعة الله.

in_urdu.name: عبید
in_urdu.meaning: ملک اللطیف، خادمِ حق، دلدلِ ایمان

in_english.name: Ubaid
in_english.meaning: Servant of Allah, obedient servant, devoted servant, faithful servant
in_english.long_meaning: Ubaid is an Arabic name that means servant of Allah, obedient servant, devoted servant, faithful servant. It is a popular name in Islamic tradition and is derived from the Arabic root word 'Ubaid', which means to serve or to obey. In the Quran, Ubaid is mentioned in Surah 9, verse 25, as a name of one of the prophets. The name Ubaid is also mentioned in the Hadith as a name of a companion of the Prophet Muhammad. In Islamic tradition, Ubaid is considered a name of great significance and is often given to children. It is believed to bring good fortune and blessings to the child. The name Ubaid is also associated with the qualities of obedience, devotion, and faithfulness. It is a name that is highly revered in Islamic tradition and is often given to children as a blessing from Allah.

data.cultural_impact: Ubaid carries a rich cultural heritage that traces back to the Early Islamic period (7th – 9th centuries CE). It was a common name in all Nigerian ethnic groups, particularly among the Hausa, Yoruba, and Igbo communities. The name represented humility, dedication, and faith in Allah, which were highly valued traits for individuals in both religious and community contexts. It was also a name that resonated with the Islamic principle of submission to God's will (Islam means submission in Arabic).
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Ubaid signifies an embodiment of the concept of submission and servitude to Allah. The name is an affirmation that the one bearing it is not only a servant of Allah but also a devotee and worshipper. As a result, it is implied that the person will prioritize their relationship with Allah and strive to live in accordance with Islamic values and teachings. The name Ubaid serves as a constant reminder of the importance of serving Allah, which in turn fosters a deep connection to the divine and a commitment to leading a virtuous life.
